questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[X].$ Give your answer rounded to two decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-1, & 2<x<3 \\ \frac{5}{12}, & 3\le x<4\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

 

We compute the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{2}^{4}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{4}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}x\cdot (\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-1)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{4}x\cdot \frac{5}{12}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{3}(\frac{{x}^{3}}{4}-x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{4}\frac{5x}{12}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})|}_{2}^{3}+{\frac{5{x}^{2}}{24}|}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{25}{16}+\frac{35}{24} \\  & =\frac{145}{48} \\  & ≈3.02,\end{aligned}
$$

 

rounded to two decimal places.

questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[X].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{1}{2x}, & 1\le x<e\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

 

We compute the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{e}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot \frac{1}{2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x}{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{x}{2}|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{e}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{2e-1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[2e-(e-1)X].$

$$
f(x)=\frac{e}{e{x}^{2}-{x}^{2}},\,1<x<e
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of expected value:

$$
\text{E}[2e-(e-1)X]=2e-(e-1)\text{E}[X]
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}x\cdot \frac{e}{e{x}^{2}-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{e}{ex-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{e}{e-1}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{e}{e-1}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{e}{e-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2e-(e-1)X] & =2e-(e-1)\text{E}[X] \\  & =2e-(e-1)\cdot \frac{e}{e-1} \\  & =2e-e \\  & =e.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[4X+2].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}, & 0<x\le 1, \\ \frac{1}{2{x}^{3}}, & x\ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of the expected value:

$$
\text{E}[4X+2]=4\text{E}[X]+2
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \frac{3}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{1}{2{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3x}{4}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{8})|}_{0}^{1}+{(-\frac{1}{2x})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =(\frac{3}{8}-0)+(0-(-\frac{1}{2})) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[4X+2] & =4\text{E}[X]+2 \\  & =4\cdot \frac{7}{8}+2 \\  & =\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{E}[12X-8].$

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}, & 0<x\le 1, \\ \frac{8}{9}, & 1\le x<2.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we simplify using the properties of the expected value:

$$
\text{E}[12X-8]=12\text{E}[X]-8
$$

For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the expected value using the following formula:

$$
\text{E}[X]={\int }_{S}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we calculate the expected value of $X$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot \frac{8}{9}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{8x}{9}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{{x}^{4}}{12})|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{4{x}^{2}}{9}|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{1}{12}-0)+(\frac{16}{9}-\frac{4}{9}) \\  & =\frac{1}{12}+\frac{4}{3} \\  & =\frac{17}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[12X-8] & =12\text{E}[X]-8 \\  & =12\cdot \frac{17}{12}-8 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$
